title: Leaked account lead to RCE
author: MoonLightLabs
summary: Public JS helper leaked account data by ID without rate limits. Valid IDs returned credentials. After ATO, .shtml upload enabled Server-Side Includes. Header-controlled SSI command execution plus encoding to bypass WAF produced RCE. Chain: leaked creds → ATO → SSI upload → RCE. Target redacted; reported and paid.

title: How a Simple Stored XSS Turned Into an Account Action Chain
author: xAbraham / hackwithabraham
summary: Rich-text event content on a community platform stored XSS after filter bypass. Same sink existed in multiple fields. Combined with an exposed CSRF token, the XSS performed an authenticated action on a test account. Fixed in 10 days; bounty after retest.

title: $5,000 Bug Bounty: Stealing Private API Keys via Arbitrary Origin Reflection in CORS
author: T4nv1
summary: HackerOne target reflected attacker Origin and set ACAO plus credentials. Dynamic origin parsing allowed reading authenticated API responses, including private API keys. $5,000 payout.

title: From a Broken Error Message to Full Server RCE: A Jinja2 SSTI Writeup ($9,000 Bounty)
author: T4nv1
summary: Flask marketing/PR SaaS rendered user campaign/landing text in Jinja2 instead of passing it as data. Error-page behavior fingerprinted the engine. Classic SSTI → sandbox escape → shell on production. Target redacted as briefinghub.io. $9,000.

title: When a Single Text File Breaks a Trust Boundary
author: julichaan
summary: An OSS tool let a marker file relocate the working directory. Resolving that file allowed path traversal outside the repo, then sync features turned the primitive into local file disclosure and arbitrary write under the user profile.

title: How I Found an Account Takeover Hiding in a Scan to Upload Button
author: chiheb
summary: QR 'scan to upload' encoded a long-lived upload URL with code/token/watchId. Intercepting instead of scanning exposed an authorization gap that enabled takeover-class impact on the seller-image flow. Program redacted.

title: How I Could Have Shut Down Every Restaurant in Europe With One Click
author: TionoX
bounty: P1 (amount not stated in public excerpt)
summary: Restaurant-partner API for delivery zones accepted swapped IDs. Authenticated partner could read and modify another restaurant's delivery areas, enabling cross-tenant disruption. PoC limited to one test restore.

title: How I Found a Critical RCE Flaw in a Popular JS Sandbox
author: Codi
summary: Directory listing exposed source maps; insecure JS sandbox in first-party utils.ts allowed RCE. Reported July 2025, patched quickly, rewarded September 2025. Vendor tried to blame a third-party Java lib.

title: GitHub Pays $100,000 Bounty for Critical RCE Flaw in Git Push Pipeline
author: Cyber Security News / Saif Ghani
summary: Unauthenticated RCE in GitHub git-push processing via crafted repository URL. Largest publicly disclosed GitHub VRP payment according to coverage. Coordinated disclosure; details limited.

title: Hacktron chained image-library exploit with OpenAI community SSO to reach internal code
author: Hacktron / SecurityWeek / TNW
summary: libheif/image-processing bug chained with OpenAI community sign-in token scope. Employee ChatGPT/Codex session used to open a harmless PR in internal monorepo as proof. OpenAI patched SSO in ~14 hours; $6,500 via Bugcrowd. Discourse/libheif patched via HackerOne.

title: How we pwned X, Vercel, Cursor, Discord via Mintlify XSS supply chain
author: hackermondev / daniel
summary: Mintlify-powered docs on customer primary domains were XSSable. Impact spanned X, Vercel, Cursor, Discord and other Mintlify customers. Combined bounties about $11k (Discord $4k plus Mintlify).

title: Inside a 14-month responsible disclosure with the RIPE NCC
author: Sasha Romijn
summary: Three RIPE reports: RIPEstat XSS via version.bind plus CSRF to RIPE Database (€1100); Atlas XSS via NSID (€100); Atlas XSS via TLS certificate fields plus CSRF to RPKI dashboard (€2000). Long disclosure, advertised bounty tiers honored.
